# netgear_lags (Data Source)

The link aggregation groups the switch has configured, read from `show running-config`.

The switch defines every LAG interface whether or not it is used, so a group left entirely at its defaults is absent here rather than listed empty.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "netgear_lags" "all" {}

output "lag_members" {
  value = { for lag in data.netgear_lags.all.lags : lag.lag_id => lag.members }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Constant `lags`. The framework requires an id.
- `lags` (Attributes List) The groups, in ascending id order. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--lags))

<a id="nestedatt--lags"></a>
### Nested Schema for `lags`

Read-Only:

- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the LAG is administratively up.
- `hash_mode` (Number) Load balance selector. Zero when the group is left at the switch default.
- `interface_id` (String) The LAG's interface id, such as `3/1`. Use this where other resources expect a port.
- `lag_id` (Number) LAG number.
- `members` (Set of String) Physical ports in the bundle, in FASTPATH notation such as `0/1`.
- `mode` (String) `lacp` for 802.3ad negotiation, or `static` for an unconditional bundle.
- `name` (String) LAG name, empty when the switch has none for it.
